tools.name: acknowledge_issue
tools.description: Mark an issue thread as an intentional choice (write scope — ask the user first): it stops counting against the score and stays marked across scans. Typical uses: noindex on pagination, a deliberately short page, a redirect that must stay. Undo with unacknowledge_issue.

tools.name: analyze_seo
tools.description: Run Seonix's deterministic SEO + readability + AI-answer (AEO) scoring on ANY draft you pass (title + HTML + meta + keyphrase). No AI credits are spent. Use it as a linter: fix the problems it lists, re-run until the score is ≥ 80, then publish.

tools.name: apply_fix
tools.description: Have Seonix apply fixes on the live site through the WordPress plugin (write scope — tell the user exactly which issue codes and get a yes first). Works for get_fix_plan items with fix_tier auto or ai_assist (wp_plugin_fixable); the site must have a connected WordPress channel. Starts a run (preview

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: The Seonix account behind this API key: email, every project with its plan, whether the MCP is available for it (paid plans only), AI/publish permissions and this month's article quota. Call this first.

tools.name: get_ai_visibility
tools.description: The latest AI Visibility snapshot: how often the brand appears in ChatGPT answers for the project's prompts, which competitors are mentioned, top cited sources. Measurement covers ChatGPT only.

tools.name: get_article
tools.description: One article with SEO title, meta description, excerpt, key takeaways, the stored SEO analysis, publications (where it is live) and optionally the full HTML.

tools.name: get_blog_integration_guide
tools.description: The Seonix skill for connecting a custom-built site or blog as a publishing channel (endpoints, payload, read routes, media, self-test, hand-over). Same text as https://seonix.ai/SKILL.md. Pass section to get one step.

tools.name: get_calendar
tools.description: Calendar slots for a month: planned / writing / completed / failed, kind create or optimize, source manual or autopilot, linked article ids.

tools.name: get_cluster
tools.description: One cluster with its member keywords, the site pages already covering it, the live SERP snapshot status and the competitor insights Seonix extracted (must-mention entities, recommended blocks, topical coverage, gaps).

tools.name: get_fix_plan
tools.description: An ordered, implementable plan for every open problem: what to change, where (page / site-wide / theme), on which URLs, with the target example. Returned as structured items; pass include_markdown=true to also get a Markdown checklist in the `[HIGH] Title — Location / Issue / Fix` format. Pages with

tools.name: get_fix_run
tools.description: Status and outcome of an apply_fix run: counts (applied / already correct / no-op / errors) and the per-item results with the before and after values.

tools.name: get_issue
tools.description: One issue with the evidence the scanner captured on the page (the offending tag, heading outline, redirect chain, JSON-LD block…) and the remediation profile: why it matters, bad vs good example, how-to-fix steps, whether Seonix can fix it through the WordPress plugin.

tools.name: get_plan_status
tools.description: Plan and entitlements for one project: whether the MCP is available, AI generation and publishing permissions, article quota used/limit, and the upgrade link when the project is on Free.

tools.name: get_playbook
tools.description: Read one Seonix playbook by name (same text as the prompt of that name) — for clients that do not surface MCP prompts.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: One project: site URL, language, autopilot mode and cadence, Search Console connection, publishing channels, plan and quota, SEO progress level, dashboard links. Paid plans only.

tools.name: get_remediation_profile
tools.description: The Seonix remediation profile for an issue code (no project needed): why it matters, bad/good example, fix steps, fix tier, warnings. Use when you meet an unfamiliar code.

tools.name: get_results
tools.description: Proof-of-ranking ledger: for each published article, Search Console clicks / impressions / position now vs the previous period, with trend. Requires Search Console.

tools.name: get_scan_status
tools.description: Progress of one scan: stage, pages found / scanned, counts, whether background probes are still pending. Poll every 5–10 seconds while status is not completed.

tools.name: get_seo_progress
tools.description: The project's SEO Progress ladder: current level and stage, what the next level requires (published articles, quality, Search Console, cluster coverage) and the publishing cadence Seonix recommends for this level.

tools.name: get_site_dna
tools.description: The project's brand profile Seonix extracted and the owner refined: what the business does, audience, tone, language, writing instructions, topics to avoid — plus the ready-to-use prompt block. Read it before writing or rewriting anything for the site.

tools.name: get_site_health
tools.description: Site Health for a project: overall score, the four pillars (SEO, AI search, speed, technical), counts of active / fixed / came-back problems, the top open problems by priority, the last scan and the next scheduled check. Start here for any "what's wrong with my site" question.

tools.name: gsc_coverage
tools.description: Indexing coverage Seonix collected from Search Console: indexed / not indexed / unknown counts, sitemap status, and the pages that are not indexed with Google's verdict.

tools.name: gsc_impact
tools.description: Seonix's own impact estimate: current vs potential traffic, keyword coverage, article impacts and top keyword opportunities.

tools.name: gsc_opportunities
tools.description: Keywords already ranking in a position band (default 4–20) with impressions, ordered by the traffic Seonix estimates they would bring at the target position. The classic striking-distance list: refresh those pages first.

tools.name: gsc_page_queries
tools.description: The queries one page ranks for (Search Console page+query report filtered to that URL). Use it before rewriting a page's title, meta description or headings.

tools.name: gsc_status
tools.description: Whether Google Search Console is connected for the project, which property, and the last date with published data. Call before other gsc_* tools.

tools.name: gsc_timeseries
tools.description: Daily clicks, impressions, average position and potential traffic for the last N days (7–90), plus the previous-period average position for comparison.

tools.name: gsc_top_pages
tools.description: Top landing pages from Search Console for the window: clicks, impressions, CTR, average position.

tools.name: gsc_top_queries
tools.description: Top search queries from Search Console for the window: clicks, impressions, CTR, average position.

tools.name: list_articles
tools.description: Articles in the project (Seonix-generated and imported): status, scores, keyphrase, cluster, publish dates. Paginated.

tools.name: list_channels
tools.description: Connected publishing channels (WordPress, Ghost, Webflow, Shopify, Wix, Custom API) with status. A project needs a connected channel before anything can be published.

tools.name: list_clusters
tools.description: Topic clusters (one target page each) with primary keyword, intent, page type, priority, volume, Search Console impressions and winnability. The content plan is built from these.

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description: Persistent issue threads (one per problem per page) with status open / solved / regressed, filterable by code, URL and status. Paginated. Each item carries the issue id for get_issue.

tools.name: list_keyword_candidates
tools.description: Keywords Seonix researched for the project (seed AI, planner, Search Console, autocomplete, user-added) with volume, competition, Search Console numbers and cluster membership. Paginated; filter by status and substring.

tools.name: list_playbooks
tools.description: The Seonix playbooks (step-by-step procedures that tell you which tools to call): promote a site, work through a page, fix issues in code, keyword map, internal links, write an article, striking distance, monthly report, connect a blog. Use get_playbook to read one.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Projects (websites) in the account with id, slug, name and site URL. Use the id or slug as project_id in other tools.

tools.name: list_scans
tools.description: Recent site scans with status, pages scanned and severity counts.

tools.name: rollback_fix
tools.description: Reverse the changes an apply_fix run made on the live site, restoring the values the plugin snapshotted before applying (write scope — ask the user first).

tools.name: score_article
tools.description: Re-run the SEO + readability scoring on an article already in Seonix (no changes saved) and list its problems.

tools.name: start_scan
tools.description: Start a fresh Site Health scan of the project's site (write scope — ask the user first). Returns the scan id; poll get_scan_status every 10 seconds until status is completed, then call get_site_health / get_fix_plan to see what cleared. One scan at a time per project; the plan's page budget applies.

tools.name: unacknowledge_issue
tools.description: Remove the intentional mark from an issue thread so it is scored and counted again (write scope).

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "list_issues" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: project_id, status, code, url, limit, offset

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: apply_fix, get_account, get_article, get_fix_plan, get_issue, get_project, get_remediation_profile, gsc_page_queries, list_issues, list_playbooks, list_projects · Private data: get_account · Public sink: analyze_seo, get_account, list_articles · Destructive: analyze_seo, apply_fix, get_fix_plan, get_fix_run, rollback_fix, score_article, unacknowledge_issue.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: apply_fix, get_account, get_article, get_fix_plan, get_issue, get_project, get_remediation_profile, gsc_page_queries, list_issues, list_playbooks, list_projects · Private data: get_account · Public sink: analyze_seo, get_account, list_articles · Destructive: analyze_seo, apply_fix, get_fix_plan, get_fix_run, rollback_fix, score_article, unacknowledge_issue

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
